cards.narration: Dev is baking muffins. The recipe needs 2/3 cup of milk. But his measuring cup only has marks for sixths. Can he still measure the right amount?
Dev splits each third into 2 equal parts. The cup now has 6 parts, so 2 thirds becomes 4 sixths. The amount of milk is the same. Only the number of parts changed.
Here is the rule. Multiply the numerator and the denominator by the same number, and you get an equivalent fraction. Divide both by a number that goes into each evenly, and you get one too.
Next, Dev needs 7 scoops of flour. Each scoop is 1/4 cup. That is 7/4 cups. Seven fourths is an improper fraction, because the numerator is bigger than the denominator.
Every 4 fourths make 1 whole cup. Divide 7 by 4. You get 1 whole, with 3 fourths left over. So 7/4 is equal to the mixed number 1 3/4.
To go back, multiply the whole number by the denominator, then add the numerator. For 1 3/4, that is 1 × 4 + 3 = 7. So the improper fraction is 7/4.
Now you can switch between equivalent fractions, improper fractions, and mixed numbers. Let's practise with Dev's kitchen.
Priya is baking cookies. One recipe needs 5/8 cup of sugar. Another recipe needs 3/8 cup. Which recipe uses more sugar?
The denominators match, so the pieces are the same size. Just compare the numerators. Five eighths is greater than three eighths.
Next, Priya compares 3/4 cup and 3/8 cup. The numerators match this time. Fourths are bigger pieces than eighths, so 3/4 is greater than 3/8.
cards.text: Same numerator: the smaller denominator is greater

cards.narration: Benchmarks help. Half of 8 is 4, so 3/8 is less than 1/2. Half of 6 is 3, so 5/6 is more than 1/2. That makes 5/6 greater than 3/8.
A fraction with a numerator bigger than its denominator is more than 1 whole. So 7/4 is greater than 5/6, because 7/4 is over 1 and 5/6 is under 1.
To compare 9/4 and 10/6, change both to mixed numbers. 9/4 is 2 1/4. 10/6 is 1 4/6. Compare the whole numbers first. 2 is greater than 1, so 9/4 is greater.
To put fractions in order, use benchmarks like 0, 1/2, 1, and 2. Place each fraction near one of them. Now try some on your own.
Dana runs the 100 metre sprint. Her coach records each time in seconds. Today the stopwatch reads 12.45. How do we read that number?
The first digit after the dot counts tenths. The second digit counts hundredths. So 12.45 is 12 ones, 4 tenths, and 5 hundredths.
Money helps. A dollar splits into 10 dimes, and each dime is 1 tenth. Each dime is also 10 pennies, so 1 tenth equals 10 hundredths.
Dana's rival, Leo, ran 12.5 seconds. Add a zero in the hundredths place to get 12.50. The value does not change. Now both times use hundredths.
Compare 12.45 and 12.50. That is 45 hundredths against 50 hundredths. Since 45 is less than 50, Dana's time is smaller. She ran faster.
To compare decimals, start with the whole numbers. If they match, compare tenths, then hundredths. Adding zeros helps you line them up. Now try some on your own.
Sam keeps stats for his basketball team. In one game he made 1 of his 4 free throws. As a fraction, that is 1/4.
His coach likes percents. The word percent means out of 100. So 1% is 1 out of 100. That is the fraction 1/100, or the decimal 0.01.
To change 1/4 into a percent, make the denominator 100. Multiply 4 by 25 to get 100. Multiply the numerator by 25 too. So 1/4 is equivalent to 25/100.
Now read 25/100 three ways. It is 25 hundredths, so the decimal is 0.25. It is 25 out of 100, so the percent is 25%.
You can also divide the numerator by the denominator. 1 ÷ 4 equals 0.25. That matches. Both ways name the same amount.
Try 4/5. Multiply the numerator and the denominator by 20. You get 80/100. So 4/5 is 0.80, or 80%.
A fraction, a decimal, and a percent can all name one amount. Let's practise changing between them.
Jordan's team bakes a pan of brownies. It is cut into 8 equal pieces. Jordan eats 3 of them. That is 3 eighths of the pan.
Then Sam eats 2 more pieces. All the pieces are the same size, so we can just count them. 3 eighths plus 2 eighths is 5 eighths.
Notice that the denominator stays 8. It names the size of each piece. Only the numerator changes, because the numerator counts how many pieces we have.
cards.text: Add the numerators. Keep the denominator.

cards.narration: Sums can pass one whole. Ana has 3 fourths of a pizza, and she gets 2 fourths more. That is 5 fourths, which is one whole pizza and one more fourth.
Subtracting works the same way. A pan has 7 eighths left, and the team eats 4 eighths. Take away 4 pieces from 7 pieces. That leaves 3 eighths.
When the denominators match, you add or subtract the numerators and keep the denominator. Now try some on your own.
Priya is making granola. Her scoop holds exactly 1/3 cup of oats. That is a unit fraction, because the numerator is 1. The denominator, 3, tells us three scoops make one whole cup.
Priya fills the scoop 4 times. That is 4 groups of 1/3. We can add them: 1/3 + 1/3 + 1/3 + 1/3.
Add the numerators: 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 is 4. The denominator stays 3, because every piece is still a third. So 4 × 1/3 equals 4/3, or 1 1/3 cups.
Now flip the question. Priya wants to fill 4 whole cups using the same scoop. How many scoops of 1/3 fit in 4 wholes? Start with one cup. It takes 3 scoops.
Four cups need four times as many scoops. That is 4 × 3, which is 12. So 4 ÷ 1/3 equals 12.
Here is the pattern. Multiplying a whole number by 1/3 gives that many thirds. Dividing a whole number by 1/3 means multiplying by the denominator, 3. Ready to practise?

items.narration: Which fraction is equivalent to 1/2: 2/4, 2/3, 1/3, or 3/4?
items.why: Multiply the numerator and denominator of 1/2 by 2. You get 2/4, which is the same amount.

items.narration: The fraction 1/2 is equivalent to a fraction with 4 as the denominator. Type the missing numerator.
items.why: To change 2 into 4, multiply by 2. Do the same to the numerator: 1 × 2 = 2.

items.narration: Move the frog to 3/2 on the number line.
items.why: Count halves from zero: 1/2, 2/2, 3/2. Three halves is the same as 1 1/2.

items.narration: Which mixed number equals 5/4: 1 1/4, 1 1/2, 2 1/4, or 1 3/4?
items.why: Divide 5 by 4. That is 1 whole with 1 fourth left over, so 5/4 is 1 1/4.

items.narration: Dev has 6/3 of a cup of water. That is the same as how many whole cups?
items.why: Divide the numerator by the denominator. 6 ÷ 3 = 2, so 6/3 is 2 whole cups.

items.narration: A player made 3/4 of her free throws. Which fraction is equivalent to 3/4: 6/8, 6/9, 4/6, or 3/8?
items.why: Multiply 3 and 4 by 2. You get 6/8. The other fractions name different amounts.

items.narration: The fraction 2/3 is equivalent to a fraction with 12 as the denominator. Type the missing numerator.
items.why: To change 3 into 12, multiply by 4. Do the same to the numerator: 2 × 4 = 8.

items.narration: Move the frog to 7/4 on the number line.
items.why: Count fourths from zero. Four fourths bring you to 1, and 3 more fourths bring you to 1 3/4.

items.narration: Which improper fraction equals the mixed number 2 1/3: 5/3, 7/3, 2/3, or 8/3?
items.why: Multiply the whole number by the denominator: 2 × 3 = 6. Then add the numerator 1 to get 7/3.

items.narration: Dev has 9 scoops of sugar, and each scoop is 1/4 cup. That is 9/4 cups. How many whole cups is that?
items.why: Four fourths make 1 whole. Divide 9 by 4 to get 2 wholes, with 1 fourth left over.

items.narration: One player made 6 of 8 shots. Another made 9 of 12 shots. Are the fractions 6/8 and 9/12 equivalent? Yes or No?
items.why: Divide 6 and 8 by 2 to get 3/4. Divide 9 and 12 by 3 to get 3/4. Both are the same amount.

items.narration: Change 17/5 to a mixed number. What is the numerator of the fraction part?
items.why: Divide 17 by 5. You get 3 wholes, since 3 × 5 = 15. The remainder, 17 - 15 = 2, is the numerator.

items.narration: Move the frog to 22/8 on the number line.
items.why: Divide 22 by 8 to get 2 wholes and 6 eighths left. Since 6/8 is 3/4, the frog goes to 2 3/4.

items.narration: Change the mixed number 3 5/6 to an improper fraction. Type the numerator.
items.why: Multiply the whole number by the denominator: 3 × 6 = 18. Then add the numerator: 18 + 5 = 23.

items.narration: Move the frog to the fraction 9/12 on the number line. It is equivalent to a fraction in fourths.
items.why: Divide 9 and 12 by 3. That gives 3/4. Count 3 fourths from zero.

items.narration: Which is greater, 3/8 or 5/8?
items.why: The denominators match, so compare the numerators. 5 is more than 3, so 5/8 is greater than 3/8.

items.narration: Which is greater, 2/3 or 2/6?
items.why: The numerators match, so look at the denominators. Thirds are bigger pieces than sixths, so 2/3 is greater than 2/6.

items.narration: Move the frog to 3/4.
items.why: The line from 0 to 1 is cut into fourths. Count 3 jumps of one fourth from 0 to land on 3/4.

items.narration: Think of 9/4 as a mixed number. What is its whole number part?
items.why: 4 fourths make 1 whole. 8 fourths make 2 wholes, and 1 fourth is left over. So 9/4 is 2 1/4.

items.narration: Is 3/8 less than 1/2 or more than 1/2?
items.why: Half of 8 is 4, so 4/8 equals 1/2. Since 3 is less than 4, 3/8 is less than 1/2.

items.narration: Which is greater, 5/6 or 3/8?
items.why: Half of 6 is 3, so 5/6 is more than 1/2. Half of 8 is 4, so 3/8 is less than 1/2. That makes 5/6 greater.

items.narration: Which is greatest, 1 1/2, 4/5, or 7/4?
items.why: 4/5 is less than 1 whole. 7/4 is 1 3/4. Since 1 3/4 is more than 1 1/2, 7/4 is the greatest.

items.narration: Move the frog to 5/2.
items.why: 5/2 is 5 halves, which is 2 wholes and 1 half. That is halfway between 2 and 3.

items.narration: A fraction has a denominator of 6. What is the smallest whole number numerator that makes it greater than 1/2?
items.why: Half of 6 is 3, so 3/6 equals 1/2. The next numerator, 4, makes 4/6 greater than 1/2.

items.narration: Priya walked 7/4 kilometres. Sam walked 5/4 kilometres. How many fourths farther did Priya walk?
items.why: The denominators match, so compare the numerators. 7 fourths is 2 fourths more than 5 fourths.

items.narration: Which is least, 5/2, 9/5, 9/4, or 10/6?
items.why: Change to mixed numbers: 5/2 is 2 1/2, 9/5 is 1 4/5, 9/4 is 2 1/4, and 10/6 is 1 4/6. 4/6 is less than 4/5, so 10/6 is least.

items.narration: Move the frog to 13/4.
items.why: 12 fourths make 3 wholes, and 1 fourth is left over. So 13/4 is 3 1/4, just past 3.

items.narration: Which is greater, 5/6 or 7/8?
items.why: Each is one piece short of a whole. A missing eighth is smaller than a missing sixth, so 7/8 is closer to 1 and greater.

items.narration: Put 3/4, 7/6, 1/3, and 5/3 in order from least to greatest. What is the numerator of the third fraction?
items.why: 1/3 is under 1/2, and 3/4 is under 1. 7/6 is a little over 1, and 5/3 is the largest. The third is 7/6.

items.narration: Is 11/8 greater than 3/2? Yes or no.
items.why: 3/2 is 1 1/2, which is 1 4/8. 11/8 is 1 3/8. Since 3/8 is less than 4/8, 11/8 is not greater.

items.narration: Which number equals 0.5: 0.05, 0.50, or 5.00?
items.why: 5 tenths is the same as 50 hundredths. Adding a zero after the 5 gives 0.50 and does not change the value.

items.narration: In the number 4.36, which digit is in the hundredths place? Type that digit.
items.why: The first digit after the dot is tenths, and the second is hundredths. In 4.36 the second digit is 6.

items.narration: Move the frog to 0.4 on the number line.
items.why: The line from 0 to 1 is split into 10 equal parts, each one tenth. Count 4 parts from 0 to reach 0.4.

items.narration: Which is greater, 0.6 or 0.06?
items.why: 0.6 is 60 hundredths, and 0.06 is only 6 hundredths. Since 60 is more than 6, 0.6 is greater.

items.narration: The decimal 0.3 is the same as how many hundredths? Type the number.
items.why: One tenth is 10 hundredths. So 3 tenths is 3 × 10, which is 30 hundredths, or 0.30.

items.narration: Which is least: 2.45, 2.54, or 2.4?
items.why: Think of 2.4 as 2.40. Then compare 240, 245, and 254 hundredths. The smallest is 2.40, so 2.4 is least.

items.narration: The line runs from 3.2 to 3.3 in steps of one hundredth. Move the frog to 3.25.
items.why: Each step is 1 hundredth. From 3.2, count 5 steps to reach 3.25. That is halfway to 3.3.

items.narration: Type the decimal for 75 hundredths.
items.why: Hundredths sit in the second place after the dot. 75 hundredths is 75 out of 100, so it is 0.75.

items.narration: Is 6.3 equal to 6.30? Yes or no?
items.why: 3 tenths is the same as 30 hundredths. Adding a zero in the hundredths place does not change the value, so they are equal.

items.narration: The line runs from 0 to 0.5 in steps of 5 hundredths. Move the frog to 0.35.
items.why: Each step is 5 hundredths. 0.35 is 35 hundredths, so count 7 steps from 0.

items.narration: Which number equals 4 + 0.3 + 0.07: 4.37, 4.73, or 43.7?
items.why: The 4 is ones, the 0.3 is 3 tenths, and the 0.07 is 7 hundredths. Putting the places together gives 4.37.

items.narration: A number has 5 ones, 2 tenths, and 8 hundredths. Type the number.
items.why: Ones go before the dot. Tenths come first after the dot, then hundredths. So the number is 5.28.

items.narration: Which is greatest: 3.09, 3.9, 3.19, or 3.1?
items.why: All have 3 ones. Rename them as 3.09, 3.90, 3.19, and 3.10. Now 90 hundredths is the most, so 3.9 is greatest.

items.narration: Sam has 4 loonies and 1 quarter. A loonie is 1 dollar, and a quarter is 25¢. Type the total in dollars.
items.why: 4 loonies make $4. A quarter is 25 hundredths of a dollar, or 0.25. Together that is 4.25 dollars.

items.narration: The line runs from 8 to 9 in steps of 5 hundredths. Move the frog to 8.65.
items.why: Each step is 0.05. 8.65 is 65 hundredths past 8. Counting by 5 hundredths takes 13 steps from 8.

items.narration: What percent is equal to 1/2? Is it 25%, 50%, 75%, or 100%?
items.why: Multiply the numerator and denominator of 1/2 by 50. That gives 50/100, which is 50%.

items.narration: The decimal 0.25 is equal to what percent? Type the number.
items.why: 0.25 means 25 hundredths, or 25/100. Out of 100 is percent, so it is 25%.

items.narration: Move the frog to the percent that is equal to 7/10.
items.why: 7/10 is equivalent to 70/100 because 10 times 10 is 100. So 7/10 is 70%.

items.narration: A fraction out of 100 is equal to 30%. Is it 3/100, 30/100, 13/100, or 300/100?
items.why: Percent means out of 100. So 30% is 30 out of 100, or 30/100.

items.narration: What decimal is equal to 9/100? Type the number.
items.why: 9/100 is 9 hundredths. The second digit after the dot is hundredths, so it is 0.09.

items.narration: What percent is equal to 3/5? Type the number. Hint: make the denominator 100.
items.why: Multiply 5 by 20 to get 100. Multiply 3 by 20 too. That gives 60/100, which is 60%.

items.narration: Which decimal is equal to 3/4? Is it 0.34, 0.25, 0.75, or 0.7?
items.why: Multiply 4 by 25 to get 100. Multiply 3 by 25 too. That gives 75/100, which is 0.75.

items.narration: Move the frog to the percent that is equal to 7/20.
items.why: Multiply 20 by 5 to get 100. Multiply 7 by 5 too. That gives 35/100, which is 35%.

items.narration: The decimal 0.8 is equal to a fraction with denominator 100. What is the numerator? Type the number.
items.why: 0.8 is the same as 0.80, which is 80 hundredths. So it equals 80/100.

items.narration: Dani got 18 out of 20 on a science quiz. What percent is that? Is it 80%, 85%, 90%, or 95%?
items.why: Multiply 20 by 5 to get 100. Multiply 18 by 5 too. That gives 90/100, which is 90%.

items.narration: Which amount is greatest: 55%, 7/10, 0.6, or 1/2?
items.why: Change each to hundredths. 55% is 0.55, 7/10 is 0.70, 0.6 is 0.60, and 1/2 is 0.50. The greatest is 7/10.

items.narration: Ana thinks 4/25 is equal to 14%. Is she right? Choose yes or no.
items.why: Multiply 25 by 4 to get 100. Multiply 4 by 4 too. That gives 16/100, which is 16%, not 14%.

items.narration: What decimal is equal to 9/25? Type the number.
items.why: Multiply 25 by 4 to get 100. Multiply 9 by 4 too. That gives 36/100, which is 0.36.

items.narration: Move the frog to the decimal that is equal to 13/20.
items.why: Multiply 20 by 5 to get 100. Multiply 13 by 5 too. That gives 65/100, which is 0.65.

items.narration: Mia made 33 of her 50 shots in soccer practice. What percent of her shots went in? Type the number.
items.why: Multiply 50 by 2 to get 100. Multiply 33 by 2 too. That gives 66/100, which is 66%.
The pieces are all eighths, so add the numerators: 3 + 2 = 5. The denominator stays 8, so the answer is 5/8.

items.narration: A pizza is cut into 6 equal slices. 5 sixths of it are still there. Ben eats 2 sixths. How much is left now? Is it 3/6, 7/6, 3/12, or 2/6?
items.why: Take away the pieces: 5 sixths minus 2 sixths is 3 sixths. The slices are the same size, so the denominator stays 6.

items.narration: 1 fifth plus 3 fifths equals how many fifths?
items.why: The units are both fifths. Add the counts: 1 + 3 = 4, so the answer is 4 fifths.

items.narration: A chocolate bar is cut into 10 equal pieces. The picture shows 7 tenths left. Lena eats 4 tenths. How many tenths are left?
items.why: Start with 7 pieces and take away 4. That leaves 3 pieces, so 3 tenths are left.

items.narration: The number line goes from 0 to 1 in steps of one fourth, or 0.25. Move the frog to 1/4 + 2/4.
items.why: 1 fourth plus 2 fourths is 3 fourths. Count 3 steps of one fourth from 0 to land on 0.75.

items.narration: Priya runs 4/9 of a kilometre, then 7/9 of a kilometre. How far does she run in total? Is it 3/9, 28/9, 11/9, or 11/18?
items.why: Add the numerators: 4 + 7 = 11. The denominator stays 9, so she runs 11/9 of a kilometre.

items.narration: A recipe uses 3/8 cup of sugar in the batter and 7/8 cup in the icing. The total is how many eighths of a cup?
items.why: Both amounts are counted in eighths. Add 3 + 7 = 10, so the total is 10 eighths of a cup.

items.narration: The number line goes from 0 to 2 in steps of one fourth, or 0.25. Move the frog to 7/4 - 3/4.
items.why: 7 fourths take away 3 fourths leaves 4 fourths. That is one whole, so the frog lands on 1.

items.narration: Is 5/6 + 4/6 greater than 1 whole? Yes or no?
items.why: 5 sixths plus 4 sixths is 9 sixths. One whole is 6 sixths, and 9 is more than 6, so the answer is yes.

items.narration: The number line goes from 0 to 2 in steps of one fourth, or 0.25. Move the frog to 1/4 + 5/4.
items.why: 1 fourth plus 5 fourths is 6 fourths. Count 6 steps of one fourth from 0 to land on 1.5.

items.narration: Maya ate 5/12 of a pan of brownies on Friday and 4/12 on Saturday. What fraction of the whole pan is left? Is it 9/12, 9/24, 1/12, or 3/12?
items.why: She ate 5 + 4 = 9 twelfths. The whole pan is 12 twelfths, so 12 minus 9 leaves 3 twelfths.

items.narration: In a relay, Zoe runs 5/8 of a kilometre, Omar runs 7/8, and Lee runs 4/8. What is the total distance in kilometres?
items.why: Add the numerators: 5 + 7 + 4 = 16, so the total is 16 eighths. Since 8 eighths make one whole, 16 eighths make 2.

items.narration: Sam has 2 cups of flour. Cut into sixths, that is 12 sixths. He uses 5 sixths. How many sixths of a cup are left?
items.why: Two cups is 12 sixths. Take away 5 sixths: 12 - 5 = 7, so 7 sixths of a cup are left.

items.narration: The number line goes from 0 to 3 in steps of one fourth, or 0.25. Move the frog to 1 3/4 + 3/4.
items.why: 1 3/4 is 7 fourths. Add 3 fourths to get 10 fourths, which is 2 and 2 fourths, or 2.5.

items.narration: The number line goes from 0 to 3 in steps of one fourth, or 0.25. Move the frog to 2 1/4 - 6/4.
items.why: 2 1/4 is 9 fourths. Take away 6 fourths to leave 3 fourths, which is 0.75.

items.narration: Priya adds four scoops of 1/3 cup. What is 4 × 1/3? Is it 4/3, 3/4, or 1/12?
items.why: 4 × 1/3 means four one-thirds added together. Add the numerators, 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 4, and keep the denominator 3. That gives 4/3.

items.narration: A scoop holds 1/4 cup. How many scoops does it take to fill 1 whole cup?
items.why: The denominator 4 tells us that 4 fourths make one whole. So it takes 4 scoops to fill 1 cup.

items.narration: Move the frog to 3 × 1/2. The line goes from 0 to 3 in steps of one half. Labels show decimals, so one half is 0.5.
items.why: 3 × 1/2 means three halves. Hop by one half three times: 0.5, 1, then 1.5.

items.narration: 2 × 1/5 equals how many fifths? Type the numerator.
items.why: 2 × 1/5 is two one-fifths added together. That makes 2 fifths, or 2/5, so the numerator is 2.

items.narration: How many halves fit in 2 wholes? Is it 1, 2, 3, or 4?
items.why: Each whole holds 2 halves. Two wholes hold 2 × 2, which is 4 halves.

items.narration: A trail mix scoop holds 1/3 cup. How many scoops does it take to fill 4 cups? Find 4 ÷ 1/3.
items.why: One cup takes 3 scoops. Four cups take four times as many, so 4 × 3 = 12 scoops.

items.narration: Marcus runs 1/4 kilometre each lap. He runs 5 laps. What is 5 × 1/4? Is it 1/20, 4/5, or 5/4?
items.why: Five laps of one fourth is five fourths. Add the numerators, 5 ones, and keep the denominator 4. The answer is 5/4 kilometres.

items.narration: Move the frog to 5 ÷ 1/2. That is how many halves fit in 5 wholes. The line goes from 0 to 10.
items.why: Each whole has 2 halves. Five wholes have 5 × 2 = 10 halves.

items.narration: A bottle cap holds 1/5 of a cup of water. How many caps does it take to fill 3 cups? Find 3 ÷ 1/5.
items.why: One cup holds 5 fifths. Three cups hold 3 × 5, which is 15 caps.

items.narration: Which is greater, 4 × 1/5 or 4 ÷ 1/5?
items.why: 4 × 1/5 is only 4/5, less than one whole. 4 ÷ 1/5 asks how many fifths fit in 4 wholes, and that is 4 × 5 = 20.

items.narration: A chef pours soup with a ladle that holds 1/4 litre. How many ladles does it take to fill a pot with 8 litres? Find 8 ÷ 1/4.
items.why: One litre needs 4 ladles. Eight litres need 8 × 4, which is 32 ladles.

items.narration: Move the frog to 7 × 1/4. The line goes from 0 to 3 in steps of one fourth. Labels show decimals, so one fourth is 0.25.
items.why: 7 × 1/4 is seven fourths. Seven steps of 0.25 land on 1.75, which is 1 3/4.

items.narration: A jug holds 6 litres. Maya fills it using a cup that holds 1/4 litre. How many cups does she pour? Is it 2, 10, 24, or 12?
items.why: Each litre takes 4 cups. Six litres take 6 × 4, which is 24 cups.

items.narration: Nine halves is the same as 9 × 1/2. Type the answer as a decimal.
items.why: Nine halves is 9/2. Two halves make one whole, so 9 halves make 4 wholes and one half left over, which is 4.5.

items.narration: True or false. 5 ÷ 1/8 equals 40.
items.why: One whole holds 8 eighths. Five wholes hold 5 × 8, which is 40. So the statement is true.
